A first stop before [Drum Kits Compared](drum-kit-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the jazz kit (18 / 12 / 14) is.
2. Learn how it makes its sound.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Look up famous uses.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- A small kit: **18" bass drum, 12" tom, 14" floor tom**, tuned high and open, in the style of the Gretsch "round badge" kits (style only; Wikipedia, "Gretsch", says little about its drums).
- A conventional small kit (Wikipedia, "Drum kit"): bass drum, snare, hi-hat, toms, ride. Sizes, lugs and finish here are from memory (unverified); every number of the sound model is the site's.

## How it sounds

- Smaller drums sound **higher** at the same tension (a membrane's pitch falls as it gets wider).
- No port, no muffling: the kick sings like a big tom.

"Drum kit." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_kit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_kit). Usual sizes (22" bass drum most common; 12"/13" toms, 14"/16" floor), hi-hat, ride 20", crash 16"; muffles deaden ring and overtones.

"Drum tuning." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_tuning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_tuning). 14" snare batter 220-349 Hz, resonant head 330-391 Hz, most often a fifth above; bass drum front head port about 6", less "round"; muffling.

"Gretsch." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gretsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gretsch). Founded 1883 in Brooklyn; a drum company first (the article's drum section is empty: the round-badge era is not described there).

McLean, Scott, et al. "SM Drums (Deeply Sampled Free Drums)." SFZ edition, sfzinstruments, GitHub, accessed 27 Nov. 2026. The cymbal recordings the pages play (cymbal-samples/*.m4a). Its manual: "A Zildjian series" cymbals, 14" New Beat hats, 20" Ping and 17" Thin rides, 13/15/16/17" crashes, a Wuhan 15" china. Terms, the authors' site as quoted on KVR: free royalty free use by anyone for anything.

"Vibrations of a circular membrane." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibrations_of_a_circular_membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibrations_of_a_circular_membrane). Modes of an ideal drum head at the zeros of the Bessel functions J_m.
